correctness.rationale: The two orbit descriptions and barycenters reconstruct the entire finite vertex set. Uniform-center all-contact proof applies when \(rt/(p+t)\le1\), while the mixed-orbit barycenter gives the unique minimum ball when \(rt/(p+t)\ge1\); exact distances and a positive barycentric variance certificate establish global minimax optimality for arbitrary centers. Algebra gives the squared radius, quadratic difference and strict gap. The attached standalone script checks 105 small triples by exact rational complete enumeration and certificate testing.

value.rationale: Panhandle base polytopes are natural building blocks in paving-matroid relaxations interpolating between minimal matroids and hypersimplices. Their full intrinsic outer-sphere geometry is a motivated shape invariant not supplied by the inspected enumerative source papers. The exact threshold \(p=(r-1)t\) causes a binomial-size pure-head vertex orbit to stop supporting the smallest enclosing sphere; the positive-part-squared formula measures the sharp defect across every nonminimal rank and parameter, rather than an arbitrary slice or a numerical table. The general barycentric lemma is elementary and is not presented as new.
